newsitem.title: USA: Orbit Tech board is challenged in lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Orbit Tech board is challenged in lawsuit.

text.p: Two investors in Orbit Technologies Inc have filed a suit seeking to unseat the board of five directors.

In information papers filed Monday in Delaware Chancery Court, the brothers Richard and Edgar Benveniste allege the director defendants were "duly and validly removed as directors and officers" and replaced.

Orbit president James Lahey told Reuters the dispute between the Benvenistes and Orbit began more than a year ago when the brothers refused to accept shares of stock in exchange for a defaulted investor note of about $650,000.
"They refused to discuss this with us," Lahey said.
Last year, Orbit's former chairman and then majority shareholder Adrian Joseph led a consent solicitation, later ruled invalid by a court order, that was intended to replace the Orbit board.

In the California Superior Court order dated June 17, Judge Barbara Gamer also banned Joseph from serving as an officer or director of Orbit for one year and permanently barred him from "interfering with the conduct of the business of Orbit."

The Benvenistes could not be reached for comment and their attorney had not yet returned a phone call. The lawsuit itself is not yet available from the Chancery Court, but according to information papers, the Benvenistes seek a "status quo order prohibiting the defendants from taking any actions on behalf of (Orbit) pending trial of this matter."
Orbit is a Carlsbad, California-based intellectual property holding company which acquires and licenses new technologies.
